items.title: 4.1 Differential equations: Definition, Order and Degree (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Book p. 124: Unit 4 introduction, 4.1 definition of a differential equation, six example equations (sixth printed '(iv)'), order and degree

blocks.text: Introduction

Assalam o alaikum! Aaj hum Unit 4, Differential Equations, shuru kar rahe hain. Yeh unit calculus ka woh hissa hai jo asal zindagi ke sab se zyada kaam aata hai: aabadi (population) kaise barhti hai, garam chaye kaise thandi hoti hai, bank mein paisa kaise barhta hai, aur bijli ke circuit mein current kaise chalta hai. In sab sawalon ka jawab differential equations dete hain.

Thori si tareekh (history): differential equations ka khayal sab se pehle Isaac Newton aur Gottfried Leibniz ne us waqt pesh kiya jab woh calculus bana rahe the. "Differential equation" ka naam Leibniz ne 1676 mein diya. Atharween sadi (18th century) mein Euler aur Lagrange jaise mathematicians ne in equations ki theory mein bahut bara hissa dala. Phir sadiyon tak duniya bhar ke saikron mathematicians, physicists, economists, chemists aur doosre scientists ki research ne in ke istemal (applications) aur hal karne ke tareeqon ko bahut phaila diya.

Misaal ke taur par, agar koi particle time \(t\) mein distance \(s\) tay kare, to us ki velocity \(v\) aur acceleration \(a\) in differential equations se likhi jati hain:
\[v = \dfrac{ds}{dt}\]
\[a = \dfrac{dv}{dt}\]
Is aham topic ko shuru karne ke liye hum pehle differential equation ki definition samjhenge aur phir us ki qismein (types) dekhenge.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Grade XI yaad kijiye: derivative ka matlab hai rate of change (tabdeeli ki raftaar). \(\frac{ds}{dt}\) batata hai ke distance time ke saath kitni tezi se badal raha hai, yani velocity. Aur \(\frac{dv}{dt}\) batata hai ke velocity kitni tezi se badal rahi hai, yani acceleration. Differential equation bas aisi equation hai jis mein aisa koi rate maujood ho.
Asal zindagi mein aksar humein pehle yeh maloom hota hai ke cheez kitni tezi se badal rahi hai, cheez khud baad mein maloom hoti hai. Jaise speedometer aap ko raftaar batata hai, aap ka faasla nahi. Isi liye physics, biology aur economics ke qawaneen (laws) qudrati taur par differential equations ki shakal mein likhe jate hain. Equation hal karne se woh cheez khud mil jati hai.

Kitab ki definition: aisi equation jis mein kam az kam ek derivative ho, ek dependent variable ka ek independent variable ke respect se, use differential equation kehte hain, aur khaas taur par ise ordinary differential equation kaha jata hai. Kitab yeh misaalein deti hai:

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
\(\frac{dy}{dx}\) mein \(x\) independent variable hai (jise hum apni marzi se chun sakte hain) aur \(y\) dependent variable hai (jis ki value \(x\) par depend karti hai, yani munhasir hai). "Ordinary" ka matlab: sirf ek independent variable hai, is liye sirf ordinary derivatives jaise \(\frac{dy}{dx}\), \(\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}\) aate hain. (Jin equations mein kai independent variables aur partial derivatives hon, woh aage ki classon mein parhenge.)
Yaad rakhiye: \(y = x^{2} + 1\) differential equation nahi hai, kyunke is mein koi derivative hai hi nahi. Pehchan ka asaan tareeqa: equation mein \(d\) wala koi derivative dhoondiye; mil gaya to woh differential equation hai.

(i)
\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} + y\cos y = \sin x\]
(ii)
\[\dfrac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} + xy\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^{2} = 0\]
(iii)
\[\sqrt{\dfrac{dy}{dx}} = \dfrac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}\]
(iv)
\[\dfrac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} + 1 = \cos\left(\dfrac{d^{3}y}{dx^{3}}\right)\]
(v)
\[\sqrt{xy}\,\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^{2} = \sin y\]

Upar ki chhe equations ko ghor se dekhiye. Har ek mein \(\frac{dy}{dx}\), \(\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}\) ya \(\frac{d^{3}y}{dx^{3}}\) jaisa koi derivative maujood hai, is liye yeh sab differential equations hain. Kuch mein derivative seedha likha hai, jaise (i); kuch mein us ka square aa raha hai, jaise (ii) aur (v); kisi mein derivative root ke andar hai, jaise (iii); aur kisi mein cosine ke andar, jaise (iv). Aage order aur degree ki baat karte waqt yahi farq bohat kaam aayega, is liye in shaklon ko abhi se pehchanna seekh lijiye.

(vi)

\[\dfrac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} + \dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0\]

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab chhathi (sixth) equation \(\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} + \frac{dy}{dx} = 0\) par dobara "(iv)" likhti hai. Sahi label (vi) hai, jaise humne upar likha hai. Is liye agle paragraph mein "equation (iv) ka order 3 hai" se muraad pehli (iv) hai, yani \(\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} + 1 = \cos\left(\frac{d^{3}y}{dx^{3}}\right)\). Chhathi equation (vi) ka order 2 hai.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Upar ki chhe equations mein dependent variable kaun sa hai aur independent kaun sa? (Jawab: har jagah \(y\) dependent hai aur \(x\) independent, kyunke har derivative \(\frac{d(\ )y}{dx(\ )}\) ki shakal ka hai.) Ab sochiye: kya \(\sin y = x\) differential equation hai? Nahi, kyunke is mein koi derivative nahi.

Differential equation ka order us ke andar aane wale sab se oonche (highest) derivative ka order hota hai. Kitab ke mutabiq equations (i) aur (v) ka order 1 hai, (ii) aur (iii) ka order 2 hai, aur equation (iv) ka order 3 hai. Jis differential equation ka order 1 ho use first-order differential equation kehte hain, jaise (i) aur (v).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Order kaise parhein: \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) pehla derivative hai (order 1), \(\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}\) doosra derivative (order 2), \(\frac{d^{3}y}{dx^{3}}\) teesra derivative (order 3). \(d\) ke upar aur \(dx\) par likha chhota number us derivative ka order batata hai; yeh power nahi hai. Matlab \(\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}\) ka matlab hai "\(y\) ko \(x\) ke respect se do dafa differentiate karo", na ke "\(\frac{dy}{dx}\) ka square".
Tareeqa: equation ke har derivative par nazar daliye aur sab se bara order chun lijiye. Equation (iv) mein teesra derivative cosine ke andar chhupa hua hai, lekin hai to sahi, is liye order 3 hai. Chhathi equation (vi) mein \(\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}\) aur \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) hain, is liye us ka order 2 hai.

Differential equation ki degree us ke highest-order derivative ki sab se bari power (exponent) hoti hai. Kitab ki misaal: equation (v) \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) mein ek polynomial hai, aur us ki degree 2 hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Degree tab hi maani rakhti hai jab equation apne tamam derivatives mein polynomial ho (ya polynomial banayi ja sake). Is liye yeh teen qadam yaad kar lijiye:
1. Agar kisi derivative par root (jazr) ya fractional power ho to pehle use saaf kijiye: us term ko akela kar ke dono sides ko munasib power tak le jaiye.
2. Agar koi derivative sin, cos, log ya exponential jaise function ke andar phansa ho, to degree defined nahi hoti, kyunke koi algebra use bahar nahi nikal sakta. Order phir bhi defined hota hai.
3. Ab sirf highest-order derivative ki power dekhiye; wohi degree hai. \(x\), \(y\) ya chhote derivatives ki powers ginti mein nahi aatin.
Equation (v) mein \(\sqrt{xy}\) sirf \(x\) aur \(y\) ka function hai, kisi derivative ka nahi, is liye yeh degree ko kharab nahi karta. Highest derivative \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) ka square aa raha hai, is liye degree 2 hai.

blocks.caption: Hamari banayi hui summary (kitab mein nahi chhapi); yahan \(y' = \frac{dy}{dx}\), \(y'' = \frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}\), \(y''' = \frac{d^{3}y}{dx^{3}}\)

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Table ki do mushkil lines ko tafseel se dekhte hain (yeh hamari wazahat hai, kitab mein nahi):
(iii) \(\sqrt{\frac{dy}{dx}} = \frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}\): yahan root ke andar derivative hai. Dono sides ka square lijiye:
\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \left(\dfrac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}\right)^{2}\]
Ab equation polynomial hai; highest derivative \(\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}\) ki power 2 hai, is liye order 2, degree 2.
(iv) \(\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} + 1 = \cos\left(\frac{d^{3}y}{dx^{3}}\right)\): teesra derivative cosine ke andar hai. Cosine ko kisi power se khatam nahi kiya ja sakta, is liye order 3 hai magar degree defined nahi.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: \(\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} + \left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)^{5} = 0\) ki degree kya hai? Pehle khud sochiye, phir parhiye: highest derivative \(\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}\) hai aur us ki power 1 hai, is liye degree 1 hai. Power 5 chhote derivative ki hai, woh ginti mein nahi aati.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Ab do aur lines khud check kijiye. (ii) \(\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} + xy\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)^{2} = 0\): highest derivative \(\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}\) hai, us ki power 1 hai; \(\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)^{2}\) ka square chhote derivative par hai, is liye ginti mein nahi aata. Jawab: order 2, degree 1. (vi) \(\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} + \frac{dy}{dx} = 0\): highest derivative phir \(\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}\), power 1, yani order 2, degree 1. Dekha aap ne? Degree hamesha sirf sab se oonche derivative se tay hoti hai; baqi terms sirf tamashai hain.

Ek misaal se baat aur pakki karte hain. Socheye aap ki class mein sab se lamba larka kaun hai, yeh "order" jaisa sawal hai: sab ko dekho aur sab se bara chuno. Phir us lambe larke ka wazan kitna hai, yeh "degree" jaisa sawal hai: sirf usi ek ki baat ho rahi hai, baqi larkon ke wazan se koi gharaz nahi. Bilkul isi tarah pehle highest derivative chuniye (order), phir sirf usi ki power dekhiye (degree). Aur agar woh larka kisi deewar ke peeche chhupa ho jahan se wazan maloom hi na ho sake, to kehte hain "maloom nahi", jaise derivative sin ya cos ke andar ho to degree "defined nahi" hoti hai.

blocks.title: Exam tip
blocks.text: Order aur degree ka jawab teen chhoti lines mein likhiye: (1) highest derivative ka naam, yani order; (2) koi derivative sin, e waghera ke andar ya root ke neeche to nahi; (3) zaroorat ho to root saaf kar ke highest derivative ki power, yani degree. Yeh teen lines likhne se poore marks milte hain, chahe jawab "degree defined nahi" hi kyun na ho.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Differential equation mein kam az kam ek derivative hota hai; ek hi independent variable ho to woh ordinary differential equation hai.
2. Order = sab se oonche derivative ka order.
3. Degree = usi highest derivative ki power, jab equation derivatives mein polynomial ban jaye.
4. Derivative sin, cos, log ya \(e^{(\ )}\) ke andar ho to degree defined nahi.
5. Is unit ka asal mauzoo first-order (order 1) differential equations hain.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Equation mein jo bhi sab se bari power nazar aaye use degree likh dena. \(\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} + \left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)^{5} = 0\) ki degree 1 hai, 5 nahi.
2. \(\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}\) ke "2" ko power samajhna; yeh derivative ka order hai.
3. Root saaf kiye baghair degree parh lena: \(\sqrt{\frac{dy}{dx}} = \frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}\) ki degree 2 hai, 1 nahi.
4. \(e^{y}\) ya \(\sin y\) (yeh sirf \(y\) ke functions hain, koi masla nahi) ko \(e^{dy/dx}\) ya \(\sin\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)\) (derivative function ke andar, degree defined nahi) se mila dena.
